newsitem.title: USA: Treasury' Summers criticizes U.S. House tax bill.
newsitem.headline: Treasury' Summers criticizes U.S. House tax bill.

text.p: Deputy Treasury Secretary Lawrence Summers said on Thursday that several provisions of the tax bill being considered in the House of Representatives are too complex.
"We note that the pending bill ... includes many new provisions that are complex, and some that are far too complex," Summers said in testimony prepared for a Senate subcommittee hearing.
Simplicity must be weighed with other policy goals when crafting legislation, Summers said. He did not specify which provisions he was referring to.
The administration has already rapped the bill drawn up by House Ways and Means Committee Chairman Bill Archer, saying it benefited well-off people at the expense of poorer people.
However, Summers noted with approval that the bill included 80 proposals to simplify the tax code, of which 69 were substantially derived from administration proposals.
Summers was testifying on Internal Revenue Service (IRS) reform plans before the Senate Appropriations Committee's Subcommittee on Treasury, Civil Service and General Government.
In his testimony, Summers repeated the administration opposition to a recent proposal that the IRS be governed by an outside board of private citizens serving part time.
"We believe that a private-sector board would not meet frequently enough to address the critical and complicated issues facing the bureau over the next decade," he said.
"In contrast, (Treasury) Secretary (Robert) Rubin and I are available every day," he said.

Summers also repeated Treasury's five-step plan for IRS reform, which included institutionalizing oversight, introducing new leadership, increasing flexibility, obtaining predictable funding and simplifying taxes.
